section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1980
title: 7 ## Causes of Accidental Deaths : The total accidental deaths recorded during 1980 have been classified under two broad categories: (A) accidental deaths due to natural causes like lightning, heat stroke, floods, land slides, cold and exposure and cyclone; and (B) accidental deaths due to other causes like mishaps in factories, road accidents, air crashes, house collapse and boat capsizing. Category (A) accounted for 3.2 percent of total accidental deaths recorded in 1980 in comparison to 3.6 percent in 1979. Under this category, the maximum number of deaths in 1980 were due to 'Lightning' (1,466) followed by 'Floods' (677), 'Landslides' (545), 'Heat Stroke' (516), 'Cold & Exposure' (402) and 'Cyclone' (134). Category (B) claimed 96.8 percent of the total accidental deaths registered during 1980 as against 96.4 percent registered during 1979. Under this category the maximum number of accidental deaths in 1980 were under the head 'Drowning' (26,355) followed by 'Accidental Deaths on Roads' (17,481), 'By Fire' (12,081), 'In Railways' (11,735), 'By Poisoning' (5,973), 'By Fire Arms' (1,708), 'By Animal Biting Killing' (1,577), 'By Boat Capsize' (1,401), 'By House Collapse' (1,308), 'By Snake Biting' (1,257), 'In Factories' (698), 'In Mines & Quarry Disaster' (677), 'By Explosion' (491), and 'In Air Crashes' (42). Miscellaneous causes recorded a total number of 30,388 cases during 1980 as against 29,659 cases in 1979. During 1980 'Drowning' accounted for 22.6 percent of the total accidental deaths in India, followed by 'Accidental Deaths on Roads by the Motor Vehicles' (15.0%), 'By Fire' (10.3%) and 'In Railways' (10.0%), while 26.0 percent were due to miscellaneous causes. The Statistics relating to accidental deaths under these categories are given in Table-III.
